one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window, both on 2026-10-15: the South32 shareholder vote on the AliGroup sale (12:00 AWST, before the US open; independent expert says fair and reasonable, board recommends it, so it very likely passes and moves little), and Alcoa's Q3 2026 results after the close (call 5pm EDT). Q3 will step down from Q2's $2.12 adj. EPS / $901M EBITDA: LME 3M slid to ~$3,214/t by Sep 29, the Midwest premium is $1.09/lb vs the $1.19 June record, and FOB WA alumina is ~$349-369/t near cost; management guided only small sequential items (+$10M alumina). Consensus Q3 EPS is ~ $1.52 per the supervisor, so the decline is well flagged and much of it looks priced after a ~16% September fall (50 -> 42). The Q4 outlook and any Pinjarra/refinery commentary are the swing factor. I dropped the FOMC hike-odds point from round 1 (unverified snippet). With no confident directional edge I use a near-symmetric lognormal with median $41.9 (a slight negative tilt from downside momentum and the softer quarter) and 1-month vol ~17.5%, which is the stock's usual 56%/3.5 = 16% widened a little for the earnings print.

fair_value.method: Pro forma (AliGroup closes H1 2027, before the horizon) blend: normalized combined EBITDA $2.85B x 5.0x less ~$3.27B net claims at Sep-27 (debt $5.42B - cash $0.67B + pension $0.57B - Ma'aden stake credited at $1.15B after a lock-up/mark-to-market haircut - ~$0.9B FCF) over 282.8M diluted shares = $38.8 (w 0.45); normalized EPS $3.71 x 10x + $4.1/share Ma'aden = $41.2 (w 0.35); forward-curve check at $3,200/t, EBITDA $3.5B x 5.0x = $50.3 (w 0.2). Blend ~$42, up from $40 mainly because I added the omitted Ma'aden stake.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2027E normalized pro forma EBITDA $2.85B x 5.0x = EV $14.25B; less net claims at Sep-27 $3.27B; / 282.8M diluted shares = $38.8

inputs_detail.derivation: FY2025 standalone $1,965M (OM) earned at ~$2,630/t LME, with a lower Midwest premium but higher alumina prices. Deck of $2,900/t (between GS 2027 $2,700, MS ~$2,850 and the forward curve near $3,200) is ~+$270/t vs FY25, at ~$185M per $100/t net sensitivity, about +$0.5B. Alumina ~$80/t weaker than the 2025 average on ~8-9Mt third-party alumina sales minus Pinjarra instability, about -$0.25B. Net ~$2.25B, slightly under the supervisor's $2.3B because I keep a skeptic's margin on refinery stability.

AliGroup is ~$0.86B LTM Jun-26 (pro forma $3,154M less standalone $2,293M) and ~$0.85B in FY2025 (OM). South32's memorandum cites ~6.8x through-cycle, which implies ~$0.8B. I haircut to $0.6B because Worsley makes AliGroup alumina-heavy and alumina is near cost (~$350-370/t FOB WA), and LTM was flattered by the Q2 price spike. Half of the $50M synergies is in by the horizon.

inputs_detail.input: Net LME sensitivity (basis, per supervisor request)
inputs_detail.derivation: Round 1 used gross shipments (2.7Mt x $100 = $270M). Net of LME-linked power contracts and alumina/raw-material costs that move with LME, and a Canadian 232 tariff cost that falls with price, the net flow-through is ~70%, so ~$185M standalone. AliGroup adds ~1.2Mt of aluminium (Hillside plus the Alumar share), roughly +$35M after the same netting.

Applied to normalized, not peak, EBITDA. Alcoa's historical cycle range is ~4-6x. Alcoa is paying ~6.8x through-cycle for AliGroup (memorandum), which caps it. I stay at 5.0x rather than the supervisor's 5.25x because MS's July downgrade argues consensus EBITDA needs a 33-49% cut and post-deal leverage is higher; I treat the SA bear notes only as context, not inputs.

Noncurrent marketable securities $1,360M at Jun-26. The shares stay locked until Jul 2028 (one-third after each of the 3rd/4th/5th anniversaries of the 1 Jul 2025 close), though they can be hedged or borrowed against. Q2-26 had a $123M mark-to-market loss. I apply a ~15% haircut for lock-up, Tadawul price risk and any tax on sale.

inputs_detail.input: FCF Jul-26 to Sep-27 after dividends, ticking fee and deal costs
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 FCF was $422M at peak prices. At the $2,900 deck, combined EBITDA ~$2.85B less capex ~$0.95B, interest ~$0.39B, cash tax ~$0.3B and other ~$0.15B gives ~$1.05B a year, but Q3-Q4 2026 run ahead of the deck. Less dividends ~$0.11B/yr, the 5% ticking fee and transaction costs (~$0.2B). The locked-box mechanism from 31 Mar 2026 gives Alcoa AliGroup's economics from that date (10-Q). Net ~$0.9B over 15 months, a little under the supervisor's $1.0-1.2B.
Pro forma diluted 282,790,901, including the 17,008,960 consideration shares.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Normalized pro forma 2027E EPS $3.71 x 10x = $37.1, plus Ma'aden stake $1.15B / 282.8M = $4.1 (excluded from adjusted EPS) = $41.2

inputs_detail.derivation: EBITDA $2.85B - D&A $0.95B (pro forma LTM $950M) - interest $0.39B (pro forma FY25 $395M, consistent with the $2.6B notes at 6.625-6.875%) - other ~$0.05B = $1.46B pre-tax, x (1 - 28% tax) = $1.05B / 282.8M = $3.71. H1-26 pro forma tax was only ~17%, but that was on peak earnings with loss jurisdictions; at normalized earnings, valuation-allowance jurisdictions push the rate up.
The aggregators disagree and the figure is mostly standalone and set before the September slide. MS says EPS 42-64% below consensus. My $3.71 sits between the MS-implied range and consensus.

Raised from 9x because the supervisor's double-counting point is fair: EPS is already normalized, so a mid-cycle multiple applies. ~10x matches 5.0x EV/EBITDA at ~1.1x normalized leverage. I go slightly below the supervisor's 10.5x, consistent with my 5.0x EBITDA multiple.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Forward-curve case: LME ~$3,200/t held through 2027, combined EBITDA $3.5B x 5.0x = $17.5B, less $3.27B net claims, / 282.8M = $50.3

inputs_detail.derivation: LME 3M ~$3,214/t on 29-30 Sep; the curve is near spot.
$2.85B + ~$300/t x ~$220M per $100/t = ~$3.5B, consistent with pro forma LTM $3.15B at a similar average price.
Same as the main EV/EBITDA method. Weighted 0.2 because banks (GS $2,700, MS ~$2,850) expect the curve to fade as a 2027 surplus arrives.

bear.story: The 2027 surplus arrives in force: EGA Al Taweelah is fully back by Q1 2027 (25% of cells were restarted by late August), Indonesia ramps, and MS's view that EBITDA is 33-49% below consensus proves right. LME goes to ~$2,500-2,600/t, alumina stays at cost, and the Midwest premium eases on a Canada tariff deal. Combined EBITDA ~$1.9-2.1B on ~$4B net claims (less FCF, Ma'aden marked down) at 4.5x gives ~$20-28. AliGroup was bought at the wrong point in the cycle with $2.6B of 6.6-6.9% notes.

base.story: Aluminium drifts to ~$2,850-3,000/t with a modest 2027 surplus, alumina ~$350-380/t, Pinjarra stable. AliGroup closes H1 2027; combined EBITDA ~$2.8-3.0B; net claims fall to ~$3.2B with FCF and the locked-box benefit. The stock trades at ~5x EBITDA / ~10x normalized EPS plus the Ma'aden stake.

bull.story: Gulf restarts slip, China's 45Mt cap binds and LME stocks stay thin (~240kt), so LME holds >$3,300/t and the Midwest premium stays >$1.00/lb. Combined EBITDA ~$3.7-4.0B with synergies; deleveraging is fast and Ma'aden recovers. The $60-80 sell-side targets come back into play (the CVR payout to South32 caps a little of the upside).

thesis_break_reason: At $27 the pro forma equity (282.8M shares) is ~$7.6B. With ~$3.3B of net claims after the haircut Ma'aden credit, EV is ~$10.9B, about 3.8x my $2.85B normalized combined EBITDA and ~5x trough (~$2.1B at $2,550/t). Trading there would mean the market prices a sustained LME collapse to ~$2,500 with a falling Midwest premium, a balance-sheet problem (leverage >2.5x on trough EBITDA after the $2.6B notes, rating pressure), or a failure of the AliGroup close or of the WA bauxite approvals, rather than ordinary 50%-vol noise. It is also ~14% below the 52-week low of $31.45.

reasoning: Round 2 rebuild on a pro forma basis. The supervisor showed with primary filings that (a) I left out the $1,360M Ma'aden stake (Ex.99.3 and the 10-Q), (b) the deal very likely closes before the horizon, so the right inputs are 282.8M diluted shares, $5.42B debt, $0.67B cash and $0.57B pension, and (c) applying 9x to a haircut EPS double-counts normalization. I verified the pro forma figures in Ex.99.1/99.3 myself, and the Ma'aden lock-up in the 10-Q: shares are transferable only from Jul 2028, so I credit $1.15B rather than book value. In my skeptic lane I added the MS downgrade (Jul 8: aluminium forecasts ~20% below consensus, EBITDA 33-49% and EPS 42-64% below consensus) and BofA's Underperform at $51. These support a deck below the curve and a sub-consensus EPS, but I note both targets ($51-53) sit above today's $42 price. My fair value rises from $40 to ~$42, a smaller move than the supervisor's $45 for three reasons: normalized combined EBITDA $2.85B (vs $3.0B), because I haircut AliGroup for alumina exposure; a 5.0x multiple (vs 5.25x); and a haircut Ma'aden credit with slightly lower FCF. I disagree with the supervisor on those three points and keep my view for the reasons in the derivations. I dropped the unverified FOMC hike-odds claim and no longer let the Seeking Alpha snippets move any number. The distribution is a lognormal with median ~$42.2 and sigma 0.52, with a slightly fatter left tail for leverage and trough-deck risk. Scenarios: bear $26 / base $43 / bull $64 at 25/50/25, mean ~$44. P(>=42) moves from 0.48 to ~0.50.
